items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: Not round, not an ellipse: NASA’s gravity-based model reveals Earth’s true geoid shape - Diario AS
items.summary: The new model released by the U.S. space agency distorts sea level to show variations in Earth’s gravity, helping scientists improve navigation systems and better understand the planet’s interior. Many people have been surprised by NASA’s latest visualization of Earth, which gives the planet a shape resembling a potato. Instead, it depicts **a scientific model known as the geoid**, which illustrates how the ocean’s surface would look if it were influenced **only** by gravity, without the effects of tides, currents or winds. The hills and valleys visible in the model are caused by the uneven distribution of material inside Earth. To make these tiny differences visible, **NASA exaggerated the variations by a factor of 10,000.** In reality, the changes amount to only a few dozen yards in elevation and would be impossible to detect with the naked eye. Using the model, scientists determined that the highest point in Earth’s gravitational field is located near Iceland, **where the geoid rises about 279 feet above the global average**.

items.title: Microsoft launches MAI-Cyber-1-Flash cybersecurity AI model - qz.com
items.summary: Microsoft launches MAI-Cyber-1-Flash cybersecurity AI model. # Microsoft is launching its first cybersecurity AI model at half the cost of rivals. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, paired with GPT-5.4 inside Microsoft's MDASH harness, outperforms models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI on a key benchmark. Microsoft$MSFT launched MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first cybersecurity-specialized AI model, on Monday at an event in San Francisco, alongside a new agentic security platform called Project Perception. The company says the model, when combined with OpenAI's GPT-5.4 inside its MDASH vulnerability management harness, delivers 96% on the CyberGym benchmark — 12 percentage points above Anthropic's Mythos — at 50% of the cost of Microsoft's current MDASH configuration. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is intended to shoulder the bulk of routine security work — roughly 90% of tasks — leaving GPT-5.4 to handle only the most demanding cases, the company said. Microsoftunveiled a family of seven in-house AI models in June, including the MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model from which MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is derived, as the company has moved to reduce reliance on outside model providers including OpenAI.

items.title: New airframer-engine business model needs to be ‘holistic’: Safran chief - FlightGlobal
items.summary: Airbus commercial aircraft chief Lars Wagner told investors on 21 July, in relation to a proposed next-generation single-aisle aircraft, that there was “probably a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to rebalance the business model” and to participate in the “three or four decades of aftermarket”. Wagner says a new platform presents a range to think about the actors, the business model, and new partnerships – although he says that the timeline for a new single-aisle development means specific detail would be “premature”. Airbus chief executive Guillaume Faury added that there was a window for “views and ideas on how we could also embark our engine partners on a different way of doing business…and where we could do better on tapping into the long-term value created by aircraft and engines and systems”. “Because not only do we spend a lot of money for the development of the engine – industrialisation, ramp-up, getting into service and all that – on top of that, for years and years, when we deliver engines to airframers, we do that at a loss.

items.title: Fish Audio Raises $50 Million in Funding to Build AI Voice Models - Zamin.uz
items.summary: # Fish Audio Raises $50 Million in Funding to Build AI Voice Models. Palo Alto-based startup Fish Audio has raised $50 million in early-stage funding to build AI-driven voice models. According to ixbt.com, the funding round was led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today, with contributions from a number of other venture funds. The market for AI-generated voice models is currently growing rapidly. Since launching its operations last year, the number of users utilizing the startup's open-source and hosted versions has exceeded 8 million. Dissatisfied with the lack of expressiveness in synthetic voices on the market, the specialist developed a new voice generation model using a single GPU and released it in an open-source format. Over the past year, the company has released five new models, including four speech generation models and one speech-to-text model. While the code for three of them has been published as open source, the latest S2.1 Pro model is available exclusively via a paid API.

items.title: Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush - SpaceNews
items.summary: Home / **Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush**. # Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush. * Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email. SINGAPORE — A Beijing-based startup has secured around $14 million to build a satellite constellation for tracking orbital objects, adding to China’s growing SSA sector. The development is the latest in a line of Chinese commercial SSA moves and a signal that China’s commercial space situational awareness (SSA) sector is attracting capital across multiple competing players, while also recently reaching orbit. Geovis Insighter Technology Co. Ltd., or Xingtu Cekong, a subsidiary of Chinese Academy of Sciences-linked Zhongke Xingtu, went public on the Beijing Stock Exchange in 2025 and in November announced a planned 156-satellite SSA constellation, with test satellites due in the first half of 2026 and operational satellites in 2027.

items.title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea - TechCrunch
items.summary: Runlayer, a startup that offers a secure Model Context Protocol gateway — a standard for letting AI models and agents securely pull in outside data and tools — has filed a lawsuit against HR software startup Rippling, according to the complaint seen by TechCrunch. The lawsuit is a cautionary tale for anyone selling AI infrastructure to enterprise customers, especially to other tech companies, that increasingly have the engineering muscle to just build the thing themselves. In the suit, Runlayer describes an extensive product trial conducted by Rippling as a prospective customer, during which the MCP startup shared everything from its product roadmap to its actual source code. The parties signed a mutual non-disclosure agreement and Rippling signed a product trial agreement with a clause that forbade it from copying Runlayer’s intellectual property or making derivative works, which is standard boilerplate in enterprise software trials. Runlayer says in the complaint that Rippling’s evaluation involved “nearly a year of intensive engineering collaboration.” But in the end, the two could not agree on a price, so Runlayer ended the product trial.

items.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises - TechCrunch
items.summary: # Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises. Since launching last year, the startup now has more than 8 million people using the open-source or hosted versions of its models, and generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million. To continue building on that traction, the startup on Tuesday said it has raised $52 million in a seed round that was led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today. The company has launched five models in the last year: four speech generation models and one speech-to-text model. One way the startup has built its library of voices is by asking users to submit their own voices for training its models, and compensating them if their voices are used. Creators can submit a short voice sample or a contract to prove that an uploaded voice belongs to them, and their voice will be taken off the startup’s platform in less than three minutes, she said.

items.title: Not round, not an ellipse: NASA’s gravity-based model reveals Earth’s true geoid shape - Diario AS
items.summary: The new model released by the U.S. space agency distorts sea level to show variations in Earth’s gravity, helping scientists improve navigation systems and better understand the planet’s interior. Many people have been surprised by NASA’s latest visualization of Earth, which gives the planet a shape resembling a potato. Instead, it depicts **a scientific model known as the geoid**, which illustrates how the ocean’s surface would look if it were influenced **only** by gravity, without the effects of tides, currents or winds. The hills and valleys visible in the model are caused by the uneven distribution of material inside Earth. To make these tiny differences visible, **NASA exaggerated the variations by a factor of 10,000.** In reality, the changes amount to only a few dozen yards in elevation and would be impossible to detect with the naked eye. Using the model, scientists determined that the highest point in Earth’s gravitational field is located near Iceland, **where the geoid rises about 279 feet above the global average**.

items.title: Microsoft launches MAI-Cyber-1-Flash cybersecurity AI model - qz.com
items.summary: Microsoft launches MAI-Cyber-1-Flash cybersecurity AI model. # Microsoft is launching its first cybersecurity AI model at half the cost of rivals. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, paired with GPT-5.4 inside Microsoft's MDASH harness, outperforms models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI on a key benchmark. Microsoft$MSFT launched MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first cybersecurity-specialized AI model, on Monday at an event in San Francisco, alongside a new agentic security platform called Project Perception. The company says the model, when combined with OpenAI's GPT-5.4 inside its MDASH vulnerability management harness, delivers 96% on the CyberGym benchmark — 12 percentage points above Anthropic's Mythos — at 50% of the cost of Microsoft's current MDASH configuration. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is intended to shoulder the bulk of routine security work — roughly 90% of tasks — leaving GPT-5.4 to handle only the most demanding cases, the company said. Microsoftunveiled a family of seven in-house AI models in June, including the MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model from which MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is derived, as the company has moved to reduce reliance on outside model providers including OpenAI.

items.title: Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush - SpaceNews

SINGAPORE — A Beijing-based startup has secured around $14 million to build a satellite constellation for tracking orbital objects, adding to China’s growing SSA sector. The development is the latest in a line of Chinese commercial SSA moves and a signal that China’s commercial space situational awareness (SSA) sector is attracting capital across multiple competing players, while also recently reaching orbit. Geovis Insighter Technology Co. Ltd., or Xingtu Cekong, a subsidiary of Chinese Academy of Sciences-linked Zhongke Xingtu, went public on the Beijing Stock Exchange in 2025 and in November announced a planned 156-satellite SSA constellation, with test satellites due in the first half of 2026 and operational satellites in 2027.

items.title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea - TechCrunch
items.summary: Runlayer, a startup that offers a secure Model Context Protocol gateway — a standard for letting AI models and agents securely pull in outside data and tools — has filed a lawsuit against HR software startup Rippling, according to the complaint seen by TechCrunch. The lawsuit is a cautionary tale for anyone selling AI infrastructure to enterprise customers, especially to other tech companies, that increasingly have the engineering muscle to just build the thing themselves. In the suit, Runlayer describes an extensive product trial conducted by Rippling as a prospective customer, during which the MCP startup shared everything from its product roadmap to its actual source code. The parties signed a mutual non-disclosure agreement and Rippling signed a product trial agreement with a clause that forbade it from copying Runlayer’s intellectual property or making derivative works, which is standard boilerplate in enterprise software trials. Runlayer says in the complaint that Rippling’s evaluation involved “nearly a year of intensive engineering collaboration.” But in the end, the two could not agree on a price, so Runlayer ended the product trial.

items.summary: # Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises. To continue building on that traction, the startup on Tuesday said it has raised $52 million in a seed round that was led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today. The company has launched five models in the last year: four speech generation models and one speech-to-text model. One way the startup has built its library of voices is by asking users to submit their own voices for training its models, and compensating them if their voices are used. Creators can submit a short voice sample or a contract to prove that an uploaded voice belongs to them, and their voice will be taken off the startup’s platform in less than three minutes, she said.
